newsitem.title: USA: U.S judge denies requests to block Conrail merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S judge denies requests to block Conrail merger.

text.p: A federal judge Tuesday rejected all motions by Norfolk Southern Corp. and Conrail Inc. shareholders to block the planned $8.5 billion railroad merger of Conrail and CSX Corp.

In announcing his decision, U.S. District Judge Donald Van Artsdalen said the actions by Philadelphia-based Conrail's board of directors were protected by Pennsylvania law and that the board did not violate its fiduciary duties.
Norfolk Southern attorney Steven Rothschild immediately said the Norfolk, Va.-based railroad was appealing the decision.
Parties in the case had said the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals would hear the case Wednesday before the midnight expiration of CSX's tender offer.

Norfolk Southern sued to block the first step of the merger, the tender offer by Richmond, Va.-based CSX for 19.9 percent of Conrail's shares, saying Conrail improperly entered into a merger agreement with CSX that precluded the possibilities of higher offers.
Norfolk Southern has offered $110 per share cash, or $10 billion for Conrail, against the cash-and-stock offer by CSX for the railroad.
